title: The Analects of Confucius
examples: What does ren mean in Confucianism?

explain.say: The Analects is a book of the sayings of Confucius, a teacher who lived in China from 551 to 479 BCE. He was born in the small state of Lu, near today's city of Qufu, where his temple still stands.

draw.text: Confucius: Kongzi, Master Kong, 551 to 479 BCE

explain.say: Confucius did not write the book himself. After he died, his students and their students gathered what he had said into 20 short books of conversations and sayings, often beginning, the Master said.

draw.text: Lunyu, the Chinese title, means selected sayings

explain.say: Its central idea is ren, humaneness, being truly kind to others. Ren is shown through li, the proper rituals and manners that keep relationships respectful, and through xiao, respect for parents and elders.

draw.text: Do not do to others what you would not want done to you: Analects 15.24

explain.say: The ideal person in the Analects is the junzi, the exemplary or noble person. A junzi becomes noble through character, learning and kindness, not by birth, and is contrasted with the petty person who thinks only of profit.

Confucius loved learning above all. The book opens by asking, is it not a pleasure to learn and to practise what you have learned? He also said that when three people walk together, one of them can be his teacher.

draw.value: Is it not a pleasure to learn, and to practise at the right time what you have learned?
draw.label: Analects 1.1, a common rendering

draw.text: When three walk together, one can be my teacher: Analects 7.22

explain.say: Over the centuries the Analects became one of the Four Books, the core texts that officials in China studied for government exams until 1905. Its ideas spread to Korea, Japan and Vietnam and still shape ideas about family, school and respect.

items: Following centuries: students compile the Analects
12th century: Zhu Xi groups the Four Books
1313 to 1905: Four Books central to the civil service exams
Today: read across East Asia and the world

draw.text: Scholars debate whether Confucianism is a religion or a philosophy

faq.a: A junzi is the exemplary or noble person in the Analects. Confucius taught that anyone can become a junzi through good character, learning, kindness and doing what is right, not by being born rich or royal.
asks: What does junzi mean?
What is the noble person in Confucianism?
What is a gentleman in the Analects?

faq.a: Confucius did not write it himself. His students and their followers gathered his sayings and conversations after his death, probably over several generations, into the book we have today.
asks: Did Confucius write the Analects?
Who compiled the Analects?
Who is the author of the Analects?

faq.a: The Analects is a collection of the sayings of Confucius and conversations with his students, in 20 short books. Its Chinese name, Lunyu, means selected or discussed sayings, and it is the most important text of Confucianism.
asks: What is the Lunyu?
What is in the Analects of Confucius?
What kind of book are the Analects?

faq.a: Confucius, Kongzi in Chinese, was a teacher and thinker who lived from 551 to 479 BCE in the state of Lu, in eastern China. He hoped to bring back good government and harmony through kindness, learning and respect.
asks: When did Confucius live?
Where was Confucius born?
What is Confucius famous for?

faq.q: What does ren mean in Confucianism?
faq.a: Ren means humaneness or goodness: real kindness and care for other people. Asked what ren is, Confucius answered simply, to love others.
asks: What is ren?
What is humaneness in the Analects?
What is benevolence in Confucianism?

faq.q: What does li mean in Confucianism?
faq.a: Li means ritual and proper conduct: ceremonies, manners and the right way to behave in each relationship. Confucius taught that practising li with a sincere heart trains us in respect and kindness.
asks: What is li?
Why are rituals important in Confucianism?
What is propriety in the Analects?

faq.a: Filial piety, xiao in Chinese, means love and respect for your parents and elders, caring for them and honouring them. Confucius saw it as the root of goodness, learned first in the family.
asks: What is xiao?
Why respect parents in Confucianism?
What does Confucius say about parents?

faq.q: Does Confucius have a Golden Rule?
faq.a: Yes. Asked for one word to live by, Confucius chose shu, reciprocity, and explained: do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself. This is Analects 15.24.
asks: What is shu in Confucianism?
What does Confucius say about treating others?
Is the Golden Rule in the Analects?

faq.q: How many books are in the Analects?
faq.a: The Analects has 20 short books, or chapters, holding about 500 sayings and short conversations. Each book is named after its first words.
asks: How many chapters do the Analects have?
How long is the Analects?
How many sayings are in the Analects?

faq.a: The Four Books are the Analects, the Mencius, the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean, grouped by the scholar Zhu Xi in the 12th century. From 1313 until 1905 they were central to China's exams for government officials.
asks: What are the Confucian classics?
Why were the Analects used in exams?
Who was Zhu Xi?

faq.q: What does Confucius say about learning?
faq.a: Confucius loved learning. The book opens with the joy of learning and practising, and he said that real knowledge is knowing what you know and knowing what you do not know.
asks: Famous quotes about learning in the Analects
What did Confucius teach about education?
Why is Confucius called a great teacher?

faq.a: Scholars and believers disagree. Confucianism is mainly a way of ethics, family life and government, and Confucius said little about gods, yet it also includes rituals, honouring ancestors and temples to Confucius.
asks: Is Confucianism a philosophy or a religion?
Do people worship Confucius?
Did Confucius believe in God?

faq.q: What does the Analects say about government?
faq.a: Confucius taught that rulers should lead by good example rather than by harsh laws and punishments. He compared a virtuous ruler to the North Star, which stays in its place while all the other stars turn around it.
asks: What did Confucius think about rulers?
How should leaders behave in Confucianism?
What is government by virtue?

facts: Confucius lived from 551 to 479 BCE in the state of Lu, in eastern China.
The Analects was compiled by Confucius's students and their followers after his death, in 20 books.
Analects 15.24 says: do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself.
The Analects is one of the Four Books, central to China's civil service exams from 1313 to 1905.
Ren, humaneness, and li, ritual propriety, are two central ideas of the Analects.

quiz.why: The Analects records the sayings of Confucius as remembered and gathered by his students and their followers after his death.

wrong.0: Confucius taught by speaking; he did not write the Analects himself.
wrong.2: Laozi is the traditional author of the Tao Te Ching, a different book.

quiz.say: A girl helps her grandmother every weekend and listens carefully to her stories. Which Confucian value is she showing?
quiz.show: Caring for a grandparent shows which value?
quiz.why: Xiao, filial piety, means loving, respecting and caring for parents and elders.

wrong.1: Wu wei is a Taoist idea from the Tao Te Ching, not Confucian filial piety.
wrong.2: The Analects contrasts the junzi with the petty person who thinks only of profit.

quiz.say: Confucius said a junzi becomes noble through character and learning, not by birth. Why was this idea important in his time?
quiz.show: Why did it matter that a junzi is made, not born?

options.show: Anyone could become noble by learning
options.say: It meant anyone could become noble through learning and goodness
It meant only kings could be good

quiz.why: In a society ruled by birth, Confucius taught that goodness and learning make a person noble, opening the ideal to everyone who studies and practises virtue.

wrong.1: This is the opposite of his idea; nobility comes from character, not royal birth.
wrong.2: Confucius loved learning and taught students from many backgrounds.
